init.$comment: The option this group is already on when a listing is first asked for, named by one of this group's own option ids (the CLI refuses any other, and an empty one; a device ignores either). A group with an init has no unrestricted state: the host opens on it, sends its id like any choice, and offers no implicit All.

ids.$comment: The title's identity in the public databases, so two sources listing the same work can be told apart from two works that share a name. A TMDB id is only unique within a type, so read it with `type`. Every key is optional and a source gives only what it has; a host drops a value that does not match its pattern, and a key it does not know. Nothing reads it to merge titles yet (docs/design/2026-10-13-one-library-across-sources.md).

live.$comment: A stream with no end: a television channel. A host never saves a place in one, offers no timeline, and starts it again if it ends or drops. Absent means false, which is what a stream always was.

subtitles.$comment: Subtitle files beside the video, at most 32. A url is kept only on the stream url's own host or a host the manifest's allowedHosts names, and is fetched with the stream's headers (a subtitle has none of its own). A file that is not SRT, WebVTT or SSA/ASS, or does not load, is dropped and the video plays on.

segments.$comment: Stretches of the video a source marked, at most 32, in seconds. A segment with an unknown type, a negative start or an end not after its start is dropped and the video plays on. An absent end runs to the end of the video.

session.$comment: The source's own name for this one playback, which a host hands back verbatim as reportPlayback's session on every report about it, so a server that converted the stream knows which conversion to end. A host never keeps it past the play. One that is not a string, empty or longer than 2048 characters is dropped and the video plays on.

headers.$comment: A name is RFC 9110's token and a value is printable ASCII, space or a tab, which is what OkHttp sends and nothing else. A host refuses a stream whose headers break this, and drops such an entry from getImageHeaders while sending the rest.

pan.$comment: A cloud-drive share, redeemed by the host and never by the plugin. It carries no drive name: which client opens it is decided by the share URL's own host, so that nothing a plugin writes selects which of the host's code runs.

playbackOption.$comment: Exactly one of `stream`, `pan` or `track`, and the field names who redeems it: `stream` plays now, `pan` is redeemed by the host against the drive, `track` is redeemed by asking this same source's `getStream`. `oneOf` rather than `anyOf` because an option carrying two satisfies two branches and is refused, which is what exactly-one means. There is no `kind` field, deliberately: a kind would be a plugin-written string selecting which of the host's code runs, where a field name is read by the host's own parser and cannot be.

id.$comment: The server's own id for this option, opaque to the host and sent back as it is in a playback report. It is not the option's identity in the host: saved places do not move.

episode.$comment: The option's episode number within `season`, as the server numbers it. A host reads it only beside `season`, as the episode's numbers a skip-times database is asked by, and drops a negative one.

video.$comment: What the copy this option plays is, as stored: its picture's size and dynamic range, for the title page to say (4K, Dolby Vision). It describes the file, not what a device ends up playing. Each field is optional; a host drops a size outside the bounds and a range it does not know, keeping the rest.

subSources.$comment: The interchangeable libraries one source is made of, and which of them it is actually reading. `activeId` may name a different one to the id the host handed in — a source falls through when the chosen one cannot be reached — and is what a host shows rather than what it stores.

onImageHeadersRefused.$comment: What a source did about a refusal of the headers it last gave: whether asking again can now win a different credential. False means only the viewer can replace it, so the host stops asking.

reportPlayback.$comment: Writes the viewer's place to the server and answers nothing; an answer is ignored. Its report carries `session` when the stream being played had one, verbatim.

setPlayed.$comment: Marks a title watched or unwatched on the server and answers nothing; an answer is ignored.

getContinueWatching.$comment: The server's own continue-watching list. Each item is a summary, with `optionId` naming the option (episode) to resume when the title has several.

getStream.$comment: What a `track` token redeems to. The same `$defs/stream` an option carries directly, never another option: an option that came back could carry another token, and nothing would bound the redemption. A source that cannot produce a URL throws rather than answering without one — an absent `url` fails this schema and is reported as a malformed result, which is the sentence its author can act on.
